audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 fits 48% over 25 games, and it reconciles with the mirror at audits/top/tahmkench__galio.json, which records 49.86% from Tahm Kench's side. Both pages now agree the lane is a near-even drain-tank grind that Galio has to leave rather than win.
audit.corrected: Kept the rating; flipped Level 6 to Galio so the row matches the mirror, the packet level chart and this page's own whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late and wants.foe[2] both say Tahm Kench answers Galio's roam with 'his R (Abyssal Voyage)'. That ability is not in his kit.
audit.why: Riot's slots are An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash, Abyssal Dive, Thick Skin and Devour. Devour is the ultimate — 'Tahm Kench devours a champion for a few seconds, dealing magic damage if they are an enemy, or shielding them if they are an ally.' There is no global teleport anywhere in the kit. So the page cancels Galio's single biggest advantage with an ability that does not exist: Hero's Entrance is uncontested here, and level 6 is genuinely Galio's row rather than a wash.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Voyage removed; Devour named as the ultimate; the level-6 spike restored as Galio's, matching the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three slot and sequencing errors. (a) 'Devour (W)' — Devour is R; W is Abyssal Dive. (b) 'his Q stuns and Devour follows' — those two draw on the same resource. (c) The full layer calls Abyssal Dive 'His escape + shield'.
audit.why: Riot on An Acquired Taste: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion.' Riot on Tongue Lash: 'If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed.' The stun spends the stacks that Devour needs, so a stun and a swallow cannot be chained — the dangerous cast is the Q that applies the THIRD stack, because Devour comes straight off it. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from Tahm Kench's side. And Abyssal Dive is 'Dive down and then re-appear at target location, damaging and knocking up all enemies in an area', 21/20/19/18/17s at 1000-1200 range — a gap-closing knockup, not an escape. The shield is Thick Skin, and it converts stored damage, so a long chip trade feeds it and a burst from full does not.
audit.corrected: Watch the stack counter: two stacks plus a landed Q means Devour is next; a Q into three stacks stuns but spends them. Abyssal Dive is his engage. Burst him from full so Thick Skin has nothing banked.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Abyssal Dive with no number and mislabels it.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive 21/20/19/18/17s is by far the longest basic-ability cooldown in his kit and the only real punish window; Tongue Lash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s at 900 range and Thick Skin is 3s. Against Justice Punch at 11/10/9/8/7s, a spent Dive gives you two punches before it returns.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the cooldown block, winCon, phases[2] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer opens with 'Respect the physical damage' and 'your shield does less here', while the content layer correctly says his Q, autos and Devour are all magic.
audit.why: Riot types Devour's damage as magic explicitly. The content layer's point — that this is a rare lane where Shield of Durand's magic amplification pays off — is the correct read, and the full layer was telling the player the opposite in the two most-read strings on the page.
audit.corrected: Full layer aligned to the magic-damage read.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states Tongue Lash slows 50%, twice.
audit.why: Riot's text gives no slow percentage — 'damaging and slowing the first unit hit'. A specific number the data does not support is exactly the kind of detail a player will plan a trade around.
audit.corrected: The percentage is gone; the 900-versus-825 range gap does the same job and is verifiable.

edits.before: Drop the easy anti-mage read here — Tahm Kench is a tank, and his Q (Tongue Lash) out-ranges everything you have while slowing you 50%, so he farms and stacks An Acquired Taste on you for free at Level 1. The one thing in your favour that the lane underrates: his Q, AAs, and Devour are all MAGIC damage, so Shield of Durand's magic-amplified reduction genuinely blunts his burst once it's up — this is a rare lane where your W earns its keep. With a single ability at Level 1 you still can't engage, so concede the opener, last-hit at max Q-tornado range, and never let him sit on three stacks with your Flash down — that's when his Q stuns and Devour follows.
edits.after: Drop the easy anti-mage read here — Tahm Kench is a tank, and Tongue Lash reaches 900 against your 825 tornado while slowing you and healing him, so he farms and stacks An Acquired Taste on you for free at Level 1. The one thing the lane underrates: his Q, his autos and Devour are all MAGIC damage, so Shield of Durand's magic-amplified reduction genuinely blunts him once it's up — this is a rare lane where your W earns its keep. With a single ability at Level 1 you still can't engage, so concede the opener and last-hit at max tornado range. Watch the stack counter: the Q that lands his third stack is the one that sets up Devour.

edits.before: Level 3 is your only honest trading window: bait his Q (so you're not slowed out of range), then W-channel to ramp the taunt, release it, and dash through with E (Justice Punch) for a knockup-burst before his grey health and Q heal refund it. Don't chase past that — once your cooldowns are down he out-sustains you, and a third Acquired Taste stack means his next Q stuns into a Devour. At 6 the lane stops being about the duel: shove with Q-tornado and use Hero's Entrance to flag a sidelane or a fight while he's stuck farming. He cannot follow your global; that map pressure is where you actually beat a 48%-to-him lane.
edits.after: Level 3 is your only honest trading window: bait Tongue Lash so you aren't slowed out of range, then charge Shield of Durand, release the taunt, and dash through with Justice Punch for a knockup-burst before Thick Skin and the Q heal refund it. Don't chase past that. Read the stacks precisely — a Q that lands his THIRD An Acquired Taste stack is followed by Devour, while a Q thrown at you already on three stuns you but consumes the stacks Devour needs. At 6 the lane stops being about the duel: shove with the tornado and use Hero's Entrance to flag a sidelane while he is stuck farming.

edits.before: This half of the map is his. The grey-health passive plus Devour's flat-plus-max-HP magic chunk out-last what your tank-AP build threatens, and his Q self-heal tops him between your poke. Worse, his R (Abyssal Voyage) answers your Hero's Entrance roam, so the one edge you had earlier gets cancelled. Don't try to out-duel a fed Tahm Kench — your Shield of Durand reduction helps you survive his magic burst but won't let you kill through his sustain. Your value is being where he isn't: keep flagging Hero's Entrance into fights and let your team finish what your taunt-knockup catches, because the straight 1v1 is a loss.
edits.after: This half of the map is his. Thick Skin's grey health plus Devour's magic chunk out-last what your tank-AP build threatens, and Tongue Lash's self-heal tops him up between your poke — Grievous Wounds is the item that changes that, not more AP. But your one real edge survives: Devour is his ultimate, so he has no global at all, and Hero's Entrance stays uncontested at 180 seconds. Don't try to out-duel a fed Tahm Kench; your Shield of Durand reduction helps you survive the magic burst but will not kill through the sustain. Be where he isn't: keep flagging R into fights and let your team finish what the taunt-knockup catches.

notes: Mirror reconciled against audits/top/tahmkench__galio.json. Both sides now say: Tongue Lash 900 out-ranges Winds of War 825; Justice Punch IS a dash, 650 range, 11s at rank 1; Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1 and uncontested; Devour deals magic damage so Galio's MR and Shield of Durand both matter; and the stun and the swallow compete for the same three An Acquired Taste stacks, so the dangerous cast is the Q that applies the third stack rather than a stun-into-Devour chain. Level 6 flipped to Galio on this side to match the mirror's content chart, the packet level chart and this page's own whys[4]. TWO THINGS I COULD NOT FIX. First, 'Abyssal Voyage' was written as Tahm Kench's ultimate in two places — it is not in the current kit at all, and the claim built on it (that his global cancels Galio's roam) was removing Galio's only structural advantage in the matchup; I rewrote both, but if that name appears on other Tahm Kench pages it is wrong there too. Second, content.win[0] and win[3] read 'Skill' where the packet chart, the mirror and this page's own whys all give those rows to Tahm Kench; 'Skill' (5 chars) cannot become 'Tahm Kench' (10) inside the +/-10% band, so those two cells still disagree with everything around them. Galio's Justice Punch also still carries the bogus derived 'terrain' flag that generated a 'Galio can cut your retreat' row for Tahm Kench in _missing-interactions.json — the mirror flagged the same thing; ignored on both sides.
